items.title: 63475_Arnett Cobb oral history interview
items.q: When I got with Milton Larkin, we had a band that we billed with Milton supervising the situation

ctx.x: All right, I came back -- I was sick. I went in the hospital; I had plurisy, and Milt Larkin, after I come out of the hospital -- I was at Jefferson Davis, and I was doing mighty fine; I was waiting on people in the hospital, and walking around because I was young -- too young to die.

I come home and I get my horn out from under the bed, and go to rehearsal and my mother came over on, like, a Thursday night -- and this is unusual, and she knew I'd been through hell and high water with the illness, and I've living with my aunt at this time; her favorite sister, and Milton Larkin brought my uniform over, and let me tell you, that uniform was a white jacket and tuxedo trousers; and oh, it was sharp. I was the sharpest -- that was our uniform.
Wait just a second. What did you do in between the time you were with this stage band and Larkin? Milt Loggins? Or did you go from the stage band to Milt?
